standard_prerequisites.name: Nagata rings and finiteness of the integral closure in the fraction field
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies both the Nagata conclusion and the finiteness that makes the branch count of A equal to the number of maximal ideals of A'.

standard_prerequisites.name: P-rings for a property of formal fibres, and the criterion on maximal ideals
standard_prerequisites.use: Propagates geometric normality of the formal fibres to the auxiliary rings used in the reduction.

standard_prerequisites.name: Normality of the completion of a local ring with geometrically normal formal fibres
standard_prerequisites.use: Is what makes the minimal primes of A' tensor_A A-hat match the factors of the product decomposition.

standard_prerequisites.name: Flatness of the completion map and commutation of completion with finite extensions
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the decomposition of A'-hat and the chain of inclusions whose minimal primes are compared.

core_obligations: Conclude that A is Nagata because a normal ring is reduced and using the Nagata-local-ring lemma (proof lines 32242-32243).

Establish that A is a P-ring for the property 'geometrically normal over k', and that the same holds for every essentially finite type A-algebra, using the formal-fibres lemma, the finite-type-over-a-P-ring proposition and the maximal-ideal criterion (proof lines 32244-32249).

Reduce to the case where A is a domain: for a minimal prime q use A-hat/q A-hat = (A/q)-hat and A^h/q A^h = (A/q)^h to see that the number of branches of A is the sum of the numbers of branches of the quotients A/q, and likewise for A-hat (proof lines 32252-32259).

In the domain case, let A' be the integral closure of A in its fraction field K; use Nagata to get that A -> A' is finite, recall that the number of branches of A is the number of maximal ideals of A', and use the completion-finite-extension lemma to write A'-hat = A' tensor_A A-hat as the product over maximal ideals m' of A' of the completions (A'_{m'})-hat (proof lines 32262-32271).

Since each A'_{m'} is local with geometrically normal formal fibres, use the normality-of-completion lemma to conclude (A'_{m'})-hat is normal, so the minimal primes of A' tensor_A A-hat correspond one-to-one to the factors of the product (proof lines 32272-32277).

Use flatness of A -> A-hat to obtain A-hat subset A' tensor_A A-hat subset K tensor_A A-hat; since the outer rings have the same minimal primes, so does the middle one, a step the author states is a small detail omitted, completing the branch statement (proof lines 32278-32284).

Obtain the geometric-branches statement by applying the branch result to A^{sh}, using that the formal fibres of A^{sh} are geometrically normal and that (A^{sh})-hat = ((A-hat)^{sh})-hat (proof lines 32287-32293).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a Noetherian local ring (A, m) whose formal fibres are geometrically normal (as happens for excellent or quasi-excellent rings) and concludes both that A is Nagata and that the number of (geometric) branches of A and of its completion A-hat agree (source lines 32230-32239). The proof is a multi-stage reduction. Since a normal ring is reduced, A is Nagata by the Nagata-local-ring lemma; the rest of the proof then establishes that A is a P-ring for the property 'geometrically normal over k' using the formal-fibres lemma, the finite-type-over-a-P-ring proposition and the criterion on maximal ideals, together with the corresponding statement for essentially finite type A-algebras (proof lines 32242-32249). It then reduces to the case where A is a domain: for a minimal prime q one has A-hat/q A-hat = (A/q)-hat and A^h/q A^h = (A/q)^h, so the number of branches of A is the sum over q of the numbers of branches of the quotients, and the same for A-hat (proof lines 32252-32259). The substantive part is the domain case. Letting A' be the integral closure of A in its fraction field K, finiteness of A -> A' follows from Nagata; the number of branches of A is the number of maximal ideals of A', and A'-hat decomposes as A' tensor_A A-hat, which in turn is the product over the maximal ideals m' of A' of the completions (A'_{m'})-hat (proof lines 32262-32271). Because each A'_{m'} is a local ring with geometrically normal formal fibres, each such completion is normal, so the minimal primes of A' tensor_A A-hat are in bijection with the factors of that product (proof lines 32272-32278). Finally, flatness of A -> A-hat gives the inclusions A-hat subset A' tensor_A A-hat subset K tensor_A A-hat, and since the outer rings have the same minimal primes so does the middle one, in a step the author states is a small detail omitted, which finishes the proof (proof lines 32278-32284). The geometric-branches statement is then obtained by applying the branch result to A^{sh}, using that its formal fibres are geometrically normal and that (A^{sh})-hat = ((A-hat)^{sh})-hat (proof lines 32287-32293). The non-routine content is the P-ring reduction and the minimal-prime comparison in the domain case.
